title: Multi-session longitudinal motor imagery EEG dataset (Kumar et al. 2024)
description: A longitudinal motor imagery EEG dataset from 18 BCI-naive participants recorded across six sessions (one offline and five online) to study transfer learning for brain-computer interface skill acquisition. It compares Generic Recentering (unsupervised) and Personally Assisted Recentering (supervised) domain adaptation for calibration-free BCI training with left/right hand motor imagery and visual feedback. Data were recorded with 22 EEG channels at 512 Hz and decoded with Riemannian geometry-based classifiers.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from 18 healthy subjects over 6 sessions using ANT Neuro eego mylab hardware (22 EEG and 3 EOG channels, 512 Hz). Participants performed cue-based left/right hand motor imagery with continuous visual feedback in bar-feedback runs and car racing games. Session 1 had 4 offline runs (80 trials) and sessions 2-6 had 3-4 online runs each. Signals were bandpass filtered at 8-30 Hz (second-order Butterworth), and covariance features were classified with a Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean decoder.
